old: Workflow metrics combine exact-tier MATCH decisions, model-scored candidates, and blocking-missed positives counted as NO\_MATCH. Blocking misses are never passed through the classifier. Reported recall is \emph{decision recall}, $TP/(TP+FN)$, where FN counts positives decided NO\_MATCH (including blocking misses); positives deferred to REVIEW are excluded from this denominator and reported separately in the REVIEW column. We report precision, decision recall, F1, FP, FN, REVIEW, and $U$ as means and sample standard deviations over the three partitions.
new:
Workflow metrics combine exact-tier MATCH decisions, model-scored candidates, and blocking-missed positives assigned NO\_MATCH. Let $TP$ and $FP$ count positive and negative MATCH decisions, $FN$ count positive NO\_MATCH decisions including blocking misses, and $R_+$ count positive REVIEW decisions. REVIEW is neither an automated match nor an evaluated human correction. We preserve the original conditional metrics and add automatic end-to-end metrics:
\begin{align}
P&=\frac{TP}{TP+FP},\quad R_{\rm dec}=\frac{TP}{TP+FN},\\
R_{\rm auto}&=\frac{TP}{TP+FN+R_+},\\
F_{\rm dec}&=\frac{2TP}{2TP+FP+FN},\\
F_{\rm auto}&=\frac{2TP}{2TP+FP+FN+R_+}.
\end{align}
Decision recall excludes deferred positives; it is not end-to-end recall. A zero denominator gives zero. Review rate is REVIEW divided by the number of evaluated exact-tier plus model-scored candidates; coverage is one minus this rate. Blocking misses affect recall and loss but are not reviewable candidates. Ungenerated negative pairs are not included. We aggregate per-partition metrics with equal weights and sample SD, not a pooled confusion matrix. Full per-seed counts, SDs, and optimizer vectors accompany the reproducibility package.

\textbf{Why policy optimization mattered.} Moving from the fixed policy (B0) to validation-tuned thresholds (B1) raises recall from 0.7486 to 0.8146 and F1 from 0.8510 to 0.8910, while reducing $U$ by 499.6. Mean FN falls by 613.7, but FP rises by 27.3 and REVIEW by 593.7. The result is operational rather than uniformly better: tuning improves the declared objective and F1 by accepting more false-merge and review burden.

\textbf{What policy flexibility and GA achieved.} B1--B2 changes the policy class and its non-nested search domain. The expanded Sobol policy improves mean $U$ by only 4.5 (raw means) and lowers F1 by 0.0009, indicating a small objective-specific trade-off attributable to the combined class-and-domain change rather than added parameters alone. The expanded genetic policy obtains the lowest mean $U$, 1858.2, and F1 0.8903. However, B2 and B3 differ by only 1.8 objective points and 0.00014 F1. GA improves $U$ by 5.5 in seed 101, ties in seed 202, and is 0.1 worse in seed 303. Thus GA successfully searches the operational policy and improves substantially over fixed operation, but the controlled comparison attributes almost all gain to validation-based policy selection rather than to GA specifically.
